subject: lion
pitch: A proud old lion resting with his head held high. A huge shaggy mane fading from golden blond at the face to dark chocolate at the edges, a tawny body with a pale cream belly and muzzle, amber eyes, a broad black nose, a scar across one eyebrow, big padded paws and a long tail ending in a dark tuft.
reasoning:
I need to build a lion model using the agentic-3js-builder SDK, so I'm reviewing which API functions are available from the cheat sheet to make sure I only rely on documented methods like joint, chain, sweep, loft, and the other primitives listed.

I'm uncertain about some exact signatures, like how sweep handles radius or what paint helpers like stripes and countershade actually accept, so I'll keep usage conservative and stick to plain string colors for parts. My plan is to build the body as a chain with a tail, add a head, construct the mane as layered colored spikes or shells fading from golden to chocolate by radial position, and add separate cream-colored belly and muzzle parts.

For the finer details, I'm adding small amber spheres for eyes, a dark nose, a thin scar stick on the brow, and big paws using scaled spheres since part options support a scale property. I'm also planning a dark tuft sphere at the tail's end and settling on a sphinx-like resting pose with hips low, front legs extended forward, and the head held high, roughly sizing the lion at 2.2m long and 1.2-1.3m tall, with a root hip joint and a spine chain curving from hips to shoulders.

Now I'm working through how the body mesh gets built from that spine chain, using a sweep or loft along the path for the torso with a separate lighter sweep underneath for the cream belly, and setting up neck and head joints with a jaw, then starting on the limb function for the front legs extending forward from the shoulders.

For the mane, I'm weighing uncertain API calls — ring-based placement of spikes around the head joint versus manually scattering spike geometry using randomized surface hits — settling on a safer approach using stick/spike parts anchored to sampled points on the head surface.

Simplest robust approach: place mane tufts as cone geometry parts bound to the head bone with position and outward direction, using a gold-to-chocolate color gradient across roughly six shades to stay within the color budget. Now I'm working out concrete head and mane positioning in meters.

I'm sketching the body structure: a spine chain running from hips to shoulders with a sweep for the torso radius, a neck chain connecting chest to head, and a head joint defined with position, aim, and up vectors — all using named joint and part calls consistent with the chain/sweep API.

Now I'm detailing the head and face: a sphere for the skull, a cream muzzle, a black nose sphere, a jaw joint with its own part, amber eye spheres positioned symmetrically, and a scar across the brow built from a thin rotated box geometry.

I'm also planning rounded ears near the top-back of the head, then setting up the mane as a ring of tufts radiating outward from the head's center with randomized angles and directions to give it a shaggy, irregular look.

For coloring, I'm making the mane fade from golden blond nearest the face to dark chocolate at the outer edges, using interpolated color bands by radial distance. Each tuft is a low-poly cone positioned outward from center with slight backward tilt for a natural frame around the face.

For the body, I'm building it from sweeps: a tawny spine sweep with added chest mass near the shoulders and a cream belly path offset lower along the spine for the characteristic light underside.

For the sphinx pose, I'm planning front legs bent at the elbow with the forearm lying flat forward on the ground, using a chain of shoulder-elbow-wrist points with a tapered sweep radius, then attaching padded paw shapes at the wrist ends—though I'm unsure of the exact joint/bone API so I'll likely place paws as standalone parts without bone attachment if needed.

I'm narrowing the toolset to just createBuilder, joint, chain, sweep, and part. I set a root hip joint, assume the spine chain starts from it, then plan a drooping tail using a catmull path from the hips back and down to the ground with a tapered sweep and a dark tuft sphere at the tip.

Now I'm figuring out body proportions for the sphinx pose—spine sweep radius, chest height, neck path, and how legs reach the ground—while deciding whether spine and neck should be one continuous chain or separate ones joined at a shared point.

I'm placing the head at the neck's end joint and designing the mane as a ring of outward-facing tufts around the head center, working out the radius range and the spherical direction math for scattering each tuft.

I want to skip tufts pointing toward the face's underside so the chin stays clear of mane geometry, and color each tuft by radial band from gold near the face to darker brown toward the back using a small palette.

Writing cone geometry for tufts...

Now I'm working out facial feature placement—adding a scar box across the brow, positioning amber eye spheres so they sit mostly within the head sphere's surface but protrude slightly, and placing the nose offset forward and down from the head center.

I'm sizing the muzzle as a cream ellipsoid extending forward from the face, with the black nose sitting at its tip, and sketching the jaw as another ellipsoid beneath it. I'm realizing the jaw needs its own joint and I'm uncertain how to correctly set its parent relationship in the joint chain, since only the very first joint can lack a parent and I don't yet know what name to reference for the head's parent chain.

Looking at the cheat sheet again, there's no explicit parent option for joints — I'll assume parenting is inferred automatically from proximity to existing joints, so I'll just create "head" and "jaw" joints by position without specifying hierarchy. Now I'm sketching the physical details: padded paws as scaled spheres with darker pad accents, and positioning the front limbs symmetrically on the lion's body.

For the hind legs, I'm folding them sphinx-style with haunch spheres at the hips and paws tucked forward, using tube sweeps along point paths to form the lower legs and arms. I'm also planning the tail with a sphere tip and cone tufts, and compiling a color palette covering tawny fur, cream highlights, dark chocolate accents, amber tones, and darker pad/nose/scar colors.

Now I'm working out the tail path geometry, curving from the hips back and down to a tapered tip, with a radial tuft of angled cones plus a sphere cap at the end. I'm sketching out a mane generation loop that rings around the head, using a seeded random function and jittered angles to vary tuft direction and length based on position.

Working out leg and paw placements next — shoulder-to-forearm points for the front legs, haunch-to-hind-paw points for the back legs, each capped with ellipsoid paws and tiny toe pad spheres, checking that the lowest points sit near ground level. I'm also laying out a belly path that bulges slightly below the body's sweep for a visible cream-colored underside, and planning the head and jaw joints with aim vectors for proper orientation before writing the final code with spine, head, and jaw construction using catmull-smoothed paths.
